dublinCore.title: Regions of the Eastern Mediterranean Map
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean travel
geography
Aegean Sea
Anatolia
Greek islands
dublinCore.description: An atlas-style D3.js map of the regions, island groups, seas, and straits named in Part One of Chapter 1: Thrace, Anatolia, Ionia, Attica and Central Greece, Crete, the Cyclades, the Dodecanese, the North Aegean Islands, the Aegean Sea, the Eastern Mediterranean, the Bosphorus, and the Dardanelles. Hovering shows an infobox; clicking explores a region and checks it off a 12-item list, with a confetti cannon when all 12 are explored. A Find the Region mode hides the names and gives feedback and hints on every click. Every meaningful action is emitted as an xAPI-shaped statement and shown in an Event stream tab.

topic: Physical and historical geography of Turkey and Greece
learningObjectives: Locate the 12 key regions, island groups, seas, and straits of the Eastern Mediterranean on an unlabeled map
Name the modern country and continent of each stop on the trip route
Explain why the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles controlled the only sea passage out of the Black Sea
prerequisites: Read Part One: The Map in Chapter 1

dependencies: world-atlas@2.0.2 (Natural Earth 1:10m country outlines, public domain)

controls.label: Explore
controls.description: Hover for infoboxes and click regions to check them off the list

controls.label: Find the Region
controls.description: A 12-question challenge with the key-region names hidden

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Clear progress and return to the full map

controls.label: + / − / Home
controls.description: Zoom in, zoom out, or show the whole map; the map can also be dragged

controls.label: Checklist
controls.description: Click a region name to have the map show where it is (no credit)

controls.label: Event stream
controls.description: Shows the xAPI-shaped learning statements the sim has emitted, with a Copy JSON button

visualElements.description: Natural Earth coastlines in a conic projection: Greece and Turkey in two warm tints, island groups outlined with dashed lines, historic regions with dashed inland borders
Hover infobox with the region's type, other names, a one-line summary, and our stops
Detail panel with a fuller description, modern country, continent, and stops
A small confetti burst for each newly explored region and a confetti cannon when all 12 are found

xapi.statementShape: xAPI 1.0.3 statement objects; window event 'microsim:xapi', postMessage type 'microsim-xapi', and window.MicroSimEvents.statements()

verbs.initialized: The map loaded, or a Find challenge started
verbs.experienced: Hovered a region for at least 600 ms in Explore mode (result.duration)
verbs.interacted: Clicked a region in Explore mode (first visit or revisit), or switched modes
verbs.asked: Asked to be shown a region (checklist or Show me button)
verbs.answered: Clicked a region in Find mode (result.success, result.response, attempt number)
verbs.completed: Explored all 12 key regions, or finished the Find challenge (result.score)

recommendedUsage: self-check after reading Part One: The Map
instructionalStrategies: retrieval practice in Find the Region mode
assessmentQuestions: Which strait separates Europe from Asia at Istanbul?
Which island group lies along the southwest coast of Turkey, and which of our stops is in it?
Why is Ionia part of Anatolia but associated with ancient Greek culture?
commonMisconceptions: Ancient Greece was only in the modern country of Greece (much of it was on Anatolia's west coast)
Istanbul lies entirely in Asia (its old city is in Europe)
Every island near Greece is Greek (Gökçeada and Bozcaada are Turkish)
